title: Book One · Chapter 84: The Kitchen Sea
story:
On a wet Sunday, Mum cannot hang the washing in the yard.

Clothes hang across the room instead. Ronan ducks under one of Dad's shirts. Then he can reach his shelf.

“It has caught me,” he says.

Mum lifts the sleeve from his head. “Dad's shirt is your hat now.”

Dad is at Mr Sun's for the morning. There is no school boat lesson today. Ronan wants to try something anyway.

“Can I use the basin?”

“It is holding wet clothes.”

“The other one?”

“It is holding our clean bowls.”

He looks round the little kitchen. Every large thing is already doing a job.

Mum gives him a small bowl and a few clean bottle lids. First Mum needs the table to cut the greens. Then Ronan may use a little water there. He must put the towel underneath and clear everything before lunch.

“That is not a sea,” he says.

“This is the bowl we can use today.”

He fills the bowl. The lids float easily until he puts a tiny clean pebble in one. It drops straight down. Another lid is wider. He turns it over, but now it takes water in at once.

Mum cuts the last leaf and moves the board away.

“Can you make this one carry something?” Ronan asks.

“I need to cook.”

“You could look.”

She looks. “It is very small.”

“That is all you can say?”

“I only looked at it. I need more time.”

He feels cross. He asked Mum for help. But she was busy cooking. She needs time to think.

She gives him a scrap of paper for a boat. He folds it as carefully as he can. The corners are hard to press with wet fingers. He dries his hands and begins again.

This little boat floats. It carries one very small seed before the paper starts to soften.

Ronan counts to twenty. By thirty, the end is wet. He takes it out and puts it on a saucer.

At lunchtime, the bowl is washed and back in its place. The towel is hanging with the clothes. Dad comes home. He ducks under his own shirt too.

“It attacked me too,” Ronan says.

“That shirt keeps catching both of us.”

They eat. Ronan tells Dad about the seed and the soft paper. “How long did the boat last?” Dad asks.

“Thirty,” Ronan says.

“Thirty what?”

“I counted.”

“Fast or slowly?”

Ronan counts again in the same way. Dad counts with him. They do not say twenty at the same time.

Mum puts down her spoon. “Can I eat between your numbers? My rice will be cold.”

They all try once more, slowly together. It still is not a real measure. Ronan writes COUNTED TO THIRTY on his paper instead of thirty seconds.

Ronan wants to put his kitchen results beside the school page. Which lid went down first? Ronan forgets. “I was cooking then,” Mum says. “I did not see.” He leaves that part blank. He is not sure, so he does not choose a lid. He draws the paper boat and the single seed carefully. Dad reads the page when the bowls are done. He asks one more question about the paper. Ronan can answer that: it was thinner than the school sheet.

In the afternoon, the rain stops. They take the washing outside. Ronan puts the little boat on its saucer. He carries it to a place in the sun. The paper is soft now, but he can still see all four corners.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- we can use＝我们能使用的
- ducks under＝低头钻过
- starts to soften＝开始变软
- count＝数数

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：pebble＝小石头；seed＝种子；saucer＝碟子。

## 读句提示

**How long did the boat last?**

这只船／持续浮了／多久？这是Dad直接问的问题。

## 理解问题

1. 家里的条件怎样限制了Ronan的测试？
2. 为什么他不能把数到三十直接写成三十秒？
